### English source — DO NOT EDIT

<!-- SOURCE_TURN_003_BEGIN -->
This joke plays on the concept of a "proof by contradiction," which is a type of argument used in logical reasoning. In a proof by contradiction, one assumes that the opposite of what they want to prove is true, and then shows that this assumption leads to a logical contradiction.

In this joke, the first two logicians are using the principle of "proof by contradiction" to answer the bartender's question about whether they want beer. By saying "I don't know," they are effectively saying that they don't know whether they want beer or not, which is the opposite of what the bartender is asking. The third logician, on the other hand, goes against the assumption made by the first two logicians and simply says "Yes," indicating that they do want beer. This creates a contradiction, as the third logician has effectively proved that at least one of the logicians does want beer, despite the first two logicians saying that they don't know.
